question.problem:
The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+1}}\cdot q(t).
$$

Find the principal normal vector at the point where $t=0,$ if 

$$
\begin{aligned}q(0)=⟨0,1,1⟩,\,{q}^{′}(0)=⟨0,1,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

current_example.problem:
The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by

$$
\mathbf T(t) = \sin{t} \cdot \mathbf q(t).
$$

Find the principal normal vector at the point where $t = \dfrac{\pi}{4},$ if 

$$
\begin{aligned}q(\frac{\pi }{4})=-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,i-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,j+k,\,{q}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})=-2\,k.\end{aligned}
$$
current_example.worked_solution:
Remember that in general, the principal normal vector is given by

$$
\mathbf N(t)= \dfrac{\mathbf T'(t)}{\|\mathbf T'(t)\|}.
$$

First, we calculate $\mathbf T'(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\dfrac{\pi}{4}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot q(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\cdot q(t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(q(t)) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot q(t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot {q}^{′}(t) \\  \\ {T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\cdot q(\frac{\pi }{4})+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\cdot {q}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,i-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,j+k)+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(-2\,k) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\,i-\frac{1}{2}\,j-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of $\mathbf T'\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖ & =\sqrt{{(-\frac{1}{2})}^{2}+{(-\frac{1}{2})}^{2}+{(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{2}} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize $\mathbf T'\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve at the point where $t=\dfrac{\pi}{4}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})}{‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖} \\  & =\frac{-\frac{1}{2}\,i-\frac{1}{2}\,j-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,k}{1} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\,i-\frac{1}{2}\,j-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,k\end{aligned}
$$
